name: Kṛṣṇa (Vāsudeva)
summary: In BhG 16–18 Kṛṣṇa teaches the divine and demonic endowments, threefold faith and its expressions, oṃ tat sat, relinquishment and renunciation, the five causes of action and the guṇa-typology, the path from one's own work to entering him, and gives the 'most secret' word (18.64–66); he is called Hṛṣīkeśa, Keśiniṣūdana (18.1), Acyuta (18.73), Vāsudeva (18.74), Kṛṣṇa the lord of yoga (18.75, 18.78), Keśava (18.76) and Hari (18.77).

name: Arjuna (Pārtha, Dhanaṃjaya)
summary: In BhG 16–18 Arjuna, told he is born to the divine endowment (16.5), asks about those who sacrifice with faith outside scripture (17.1) and about saṃnyāsa and tyāga (18.1), is called dear (18.64–65), and declares his delusion destroyed and his memory regained: 'I will do your word' (18.73). Addressed as Pārtha, Kaunteya, Bhārata, Pāṇḍava, Dhanañjaya, Paraṃtapa and other epithets.

name: Sañjaya
summary: In BhG 18.74–78 Sañjaya tells the king that by Vyāsa's grace he heard the wondrous dialogue directly from Kṛṣṇa, rejoices again and again in recalling it and Hari's form, and declares that fortune and victory are where Kṛṣṇa and Arjuna are.

name: Vyāsa (Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana)
summary: BhG 18.75: by Vyāsa's grace (vyāsa-prasādāt) Sañjaya heard the supreme secret yoga from Kṛṣṇa himself.

name: Dhṛtarāṣṭra
summary: Addressed as 'king' (rājan) by Sañjaya in the Gītā's closing verses (18.76–77), answering the question with which the text opened (1.1).
